primer_leakage_audit.impact: Primer provides definition of 3 truth values, xen branch, and unwrap_or. Tasks T1-06 (anti-coercion) and T5-01/T5-02 (plain language) test semantic internalization rather than rote memorization; no solutions are given verbatim.

statistical_interpretation.xox_vs_baseline_b_d1: XoX descriptive D1 (100.0%) vs Baseline B (98.33%): In this study, no statistically significant difference was detected between XoXLang and Python Structured on semantic prediction (p = 0.079). Formal equivalence was not established because no equivalence margin was predeclared.
statistical_interpretation.xox_vs_baseline_b_d2: XoX (0/15 participants, 0.0%) vs Baseline B (2/15 participants, 13.33%): Fisher exact p = 0.4828 indicates no statistically significant difference detected. Formal equivalence was not established because no equivalence margin was predeclared.
statistical_interpretation.xox_vs_baseline_a: XoX significantly outperforms Classic Python on participant-level unsafe modification incidence (0/15 vs 8/15 participants, Fisher exact p = 0.0022; 95% CI [30.12%, 75.19%]) and on discriminating tasks (Mann-Whitney U = 217.5, p = 2.25e-6).
statistical_interpretation.zero_failure_bound_interpretation: Observed 0/15 participant failures in XoX yields a 95% Wilson upper bound of 20.39% (Clopper-Pearson 21.80%, Rule-of-Three ~20.00%). Observed zero failures does not imply zero true real-world risk.

biases_and_threats_found: Pseudoreplication in original task-level Fisher tests: Resolved by reanalyzing outcomes at the participant level (N=15 per condition).
Ceiling Effect in T2 and T5: Highly structured prompts yield high performance across all conditions in basic bug identification and plain explanation.
Cohort Generalization: Agent cohort (N=30) and human cohort (N=15) exhibit congruent trends, but small human N=5 per condition is underpowered for standalone strong statistical claims.
precise_surviving_claim: Across 45 independent participants, XoXLang showed significantly fewer participant-level unsafe modifications than Classic Python (0/15 vs 8/15, Fisher exact p = 0.0022). No statistically significant difference in unsafe modification incidence was detected between XoXLang and Structured Python (0/15 vs 2/15, p = 0.4828). On the nine discriminating comprehension tasks, XoXLang achieved a modest but statistically detectable higher participant aggregate score than Structured Python (18.00/18 vs 17.27/18, Mann-Whitney U p = 0.0035).

statistical_unit_of_analysis_audit.pseudoreplication_resolution: Corrected in inferential testing by using participant-level aggregation (e.g. participant incidence of unsafe modifications, participant-level mean/sum scores). Descriptive task-level rates are preserved separately.
